Storytold

Local creative work. Native app engines. Verified file handoffs.

A Claude Code and Codex plugin for the open-source ArtCraft Craft App Suite: one craft Skill drives fifteen local, headless Craft MCP apps (photo, vector, video, RAW, PDF, layout, spreadsheets, documents, slides, CAD, audio, motion, interface design, procedural materials and 3D texture painting) through staged copies and verified exports.

English · Deutsch · Türkçe

Thank you, ArtCraft team! Storytold is built on the Craft App Suite, which the ArtCraft team released as free, open-source software: fifteen creative apps, each written from scratch. We're grateful for their generosity. None of this integration would exist without their work.

❤️ ArtCraft team 💚

Overview

Storytold is Devsolux's local integration kit for the fifteen existing Craft CLI MCP servers. One compact craft Skill guides the host; each app keeps its own schemas, editing state, rendering and save semantics. Deterministic helpers install and pin the CLIs on explicit command, stage files, generate evidence-bound configuration and verify artifacts within stated limits.

User + Claude Code / local Codex
           │  one craft Skill; native tool discovery and approvals
           ├── stdio ── PhotoCraft, VectorCraft, FilmCraft, LightCraft
           ├── stdio ── PdfCraft, EffectCraft, DesignCraft, GridCraft
           ├── stdio ── WordCraft, DeckCraft, CADCraft, SoundCraft
           └── stdio ── FigCraft, MaterialCraft, TextureCraft
                                │
                      native engines → durable files

What it is

  • One instructional Skill, fifteen on-demand app cards and two workflow guides.
  • Fifteen direct, native stdio MCP registrations, one per app and host.
  • A standard-library Python CLI (storytold.py) that installs, verifies, pins, probes and registers the Craft CLIs, but only when you run it.

What it is not

  • No gateway MCP server, daemon, router or second AI agent.
  • No bundled binaries: installing the plugin adds guidance, the reviewed release manifest and inactive templates, never executables, permissions or running MCP processes.
  • No remote ChatGPT connector. Local Codex support is an additive packaging and configuration adaptation.
  • No OS sandbox. See Working safely and SECURITY.md.

Quick start

1. Install the plugin. Repository devsolux/storytold, plugin storytold, marketplace devsolux-storytold. Both hosts take plugin@marketplace:

claude plugin marketplace add https://github.com/devsolux/storytold
claude plugin install storytold@devsolux-storytold

codex plugin marketplace add devsolux/storytold
codex plugin add storytold@devsolux-storytold

2. Install the native apps. From a clone, or from the installed plugin directory (<home>/plugins/cache/devsolux-storytold/storytold/<version>/ under ~/.claude or ~/.codex), set up one app or all fifteen:

python3 storytold.py setup --app photocraft

python3 storytold.py setup --all --acknowledge-unconfined

3. Start a new host session and use the Skill: /storytold:craft in Claude Code, or storytold:craft from the Codex Skill picker.

python3 storytold.py doctor reports, per app, the desktop app, CLI and host registration it finds and prints the exact setup command for anything missing; the Skill offers the same command in chat when a server is not connected.

The Craft App Suite

ArtCraft Launcher installs the Craft App Suite: free, open-source creative tools from the ArtCraft team, each written from scratch in Rust and each able to stand on its own. The File access column shows how Storytold launches each app's MCP server.

App What it's for File access Code Learn more

VectorCraft Vector illustration Read/write roots GitHub Website
FilmCraft Video editing, color and sound User-wide GitHub Website
LightCraft Photo library and raw development User-wide GitHub Website
PdfCraft Reading, organizing and protecting PDFs Read/write roots GitHub Website
EffectCraft Motion graphics and visual effects Read/write roots GitHub Website
DesignCraft Page layout and publishing Read/write roots GitHub Website
GridCraft Spreadsheets and data User-wide GitHub Website
WordCraft Word processing and documents Read/write roots GitHub Website
DeckCraft Presentations and slide decks Read/write roots GitHub Website
CADCraft Computer-aided design User-wide GitHub Website
SoundCraft Audio recording and editing Read/write roots GitHub Website
FigCraft Interface design and prototyping Read/write roots GitHub Website
MaterialCraft Procedural PBR materials as node graphs Read/write roots GitHub Website
TextureCraft 3D texture painting, baking and PBR export Read/write roots GitHub Website
  • Read/write roots (eleven apps): launched with native root flags that let them read the workspace and write only its outputs/ directory. PdfCraft also keeps its single --root on the workspace; both apply. TextureCraft loading a .mcraft package starts materialcraft-cli outside those roots.
  • User-wide (four apps): launched without file-root flags, so they can read and write anything your OS user can. setup installs and registers them only with --acknowledge-unconfined; keep them for non-sensitive work or run them under OS isolation.

Setting up the native apps

Each app's MCP server is its CLI, <app>-cli. Neither the plugin nor the desktop app provides or registers it, so until it is set up the Skill correctly reports that the app's native tools aren't connected. setup supports macOS (universal), Linux x86_64 and Windows x64 and requires Python 3.11+.

What setup does

For each selected app, setup:

  1. Downloads the archive pinned for your platform in config/releases.json (the macOS CLI zip, the Linux tarball or the Windows portable zip).
  2. Checks it against that manifest and the release's own SHA256SUMS.txt, then extracts exactly the one <app>-cli.
  3. Verifies provenance (see Provenance).
  4. Stages the candidate beside the active install and runs preflight plus the official MCP SDK probe against it: initialize, tools/list and one read-only call.
  5. Promotes it only then, to ~/.local/opt/craft/bin (or %LOCALAPPDATA%\Storytold\craft\bin on Windows), and pins the binary hash in a private lock.
  6. Registers the server with every host CLI on PATH (codex mcp add, claude mcp add --scope user).

A candidate that fails any step leaves the previous binary, its pin and the registrations untouched; an upgrade interrupted between the file replace and the lock rewrite is reconciled by the next run. Re-running setup is idempotent: an app whose installed binary matches its pin and the manifest is skipped, and a matching registration is kept. Nothing runs unless you invoke it. Start a new host session afterwards.

Options

Option Effect
--app <app> / --all Select one app (repeatable) or all fifteen.
--acknowledge-unconfined Also install and register the four user-wide apps. Not evidence of isolation.
--host {codex,claude} Register with the named host only (default: every host CLI on PATH); a named host that is not on PATH fails the run.
--dry-run Preview what a real run would do per app (keep, install, upgrade, skip or refuse, a download only where one is needed, each registration) and whether it would pass (exit status 1 if not), or, with --remove, exactly what would be removed. Changes nothing.
--list Show manifest, installed, pinned and registered state, and the paths in use.
--upgrade Move an app whose pin changed to the manifest release.
--replace Re-register a same-name server that points elsewhere; the old entry is restored if the new one cannot be added.
--remove Unregister only the user-scope entries setup itself wrote (same command and arguments, app still pinned) and delete only a binary whose bytes match the lock and that no remaining registration launches, on any host; anything else is reported and left alone.
--skip-probe Register without exercising the binary, and say so.
--trust-upstream-sums Linux/Windows: proceed on the manifest and SHA256SUMS.txt when no Sigstore bundle or cosign is available; recorded in the lock.

python3 storytold.py setup --help lists the remaining path and timeout overrides. Other platforms, air-gapped machines and custom pins use the manual chain in operations: download, lock, preflight, probe, configure, register.

Provenance

On macOS the binary must be Apple-notarized by the ArtCraft team. Upstream does not code-sign Linux or Windows builds, so the daily workflow signs every pinned CLI keyless with Sigstore cosign under its own GitHub identity and commits the bundles to config/signatures.json. On Linux and Windows, setup verifies that bundle with cosign verify-blob (install cosign first) before installing; macOS verifies it too when cosign is present. Until a release has a bundle, or without cosign, --trust-upstream-sums proceeds on the manifest and SHA256SUMS.txt alone and says so in the lock.

Daily release refresh

The workflow checks every app's latest release each day, rewrites the manifest, signs new CLIs, rebuilds the plugin, runs the checks and the real setup on Linux, Windows and macOS runners, and opens one pull request on bot/releases for review (set the repository variable STORYTOLD_AUTO_MERGE=true to merge green runs automatically). A run that moves a pin also bumps Storytold's patch version and writes that release's changelog section; merging publishes the GitHub release v<version>. Users receive the new pins with the next plugin update.

Updating and removing

Update

Updating takes two steps. First, update the plugin:

claude plugin marketplace update devsolux-storytold
claude plugin update storytold@devsolux-storytold

codex plugin marketplace upgrade devsolux-storytold
codex plugin add storytold@devsolux-storytold

Codex has no plugin update: marketplace upgrade refreshes the Git snapshot and running plugin add again installs the newer version from it. A plugin update brings the Skill, docs and the refreshed release manifest; it never touches installed CLIs or host registrations, and the plugin directory now carries the new version number.

Second, move the Craft CLIs. --list shows which pins moved (manifest_commit_pinned: false); --all --upgrade re-downloads only those apps, verifies and re-probes them, and leaves registrations as they are:

python3 ~/.codex/plugins/cache/devsolux-storytold/storytold/<version>/storytold.py setup --list

python3 ~/.codex/plugins/cache/devsolux-storytold/storytold/<version>/storytold.py setup --all --upgrade --acknowledge-unconfined

When a release changes an app's launch arguments (WordCraft's root flags in 1.5.0, SoundCraft's in 1.5.2, and DeckCraft's, DesignCraft's, FigCraft's and PdfCraft's in 1.5.4), add --replace so the differing registration is re-registered; without it setup reports the difference and leaves it alone. SoundCraft honours its roots only from 0.7.0, so an older installed SoundCraft is refused until setup --app soundcraft --upgrade --replace moves it; the same holds for DeckCraft before 0.8.0, DesignCraft before 0.9.0, FigCraft before 0.7.0 and PdfCraft before 0.9.0, which refuse the flags.

Remove

python3 ~/.codex/plugins/cache/devsolux-storytold/storytold/<version>/storytold.py setup --remove --all
claude plugin uninstall storytold@devsolux-storytold
codex plugin remove storytold@devsolux-storytold

setup --remove --all first unregisters and deletes the fifteen Storytold-managed CLIs and their pins. The workspace and its outputs stay, and so does anything the lock cannot prove Storytold installed. Uninstalling the plugin alone would leave the servers registered and running.

Install from a source checkout

The generated plugins/storytold/ runtime is committed, so both hosts install straight from the public repository and nothing is built during installation. From a source checkout, make install-claude-local or make install-codex-local installs the local marketplace instead. These targets change host state; builds and tests never run them. Host packaging and installation sources are recorded in the source ledger.

Where things live

The plugin directory holds code, docs and the release manifest only. setup keeps everything it installs outside it, so a plugin update or uninstall can never delete, downgrade or swap a CLI, and one installed copy serves both hosts. python3 storytold.py setup --list prints the paths in use.

Where (macOS/Linux) Windows What Written by
~/.codex/plugins/cache/devsolux-storytold/storytold/<version>/, same under ~/.claude same under %USERPROFILE% The plugin: craft Skill, docs, storytold.py, config/releases.json, config/signatures.json. No binaries. codex plugin add / claude plugin install
~/.local/opt/craft/bin/ %LOCALAPPDATA%\Storytold\craft\bin\ The fifteen Craft CLIs (photocraft-cli … texturecraft-cli, 9–263 MB each, depending on the app and platform). Both hosts launch these, e.g. …/cadcraft-cli mcp. setup
~/.local/state/storytold/ ($XDG_STATE_HOME/storytold on Linux) %LOCALAPPDATA%\Storytold\state\ Private state: installations.lock.json (pinned hashes), evidence/ (probe receipts per app), venv/ (official MCP SDK for the probe), setup.json (recorded paths). setup
~/craft-work-storytold/ %USERPROFILE%\craft-work-storytold\ The workspace: inputs/, outputs/ (exports land here), receipts/. setup creates it; the apps fill outputs/
~/.codex/config.toml and ~/.claude.json same One user-scope MCP registration per app and host, pointing at the absolute CLI path above. codex mcp add, claude mcp add --scope user, run by setup

The complete Unix launch templates under config/ are examples only, not active host configuration. Real config generation chooses .exe on native Windows and emits concrete, validated paths rather than relying on environment expansion behaving identically across hosts. Machine-specific configuration stays out of packages.

Working safely

Every task follows the same loop:

Inspect → staged copy → native edit → preview → save/export → reopen/verify.

  • App cards. The fifteen app cards describe app-specific pitfalls: VectorCraft headless selection, LightCraft library locks, PdfCraft explicit saves, DesignCraft UTF-8 byte offsets, GridCraft typed formulas, FigCraft page-unit coordinates, media timing and offline warnings. They are source-derived hints; the connected binary supplies the operative API.
  • Cross-app work. Pass verified files, never another server's in-memory IDs. PhotoCraft can export a PNG for DesignCraft; DesignCraft can export a PDF for PdfCraft. If a stage fails, stop at the last verified artifact. No universal batch transaction, automatic write retry or hidden fallback is promised.
  • Confinement. Root flags, the Skill, probe receipts and MCP configuration are not an OS sandbox, and other host shell and file tools need appropriate permissions too. Business use requires the local gates in acceptance and the controls in SECURITY.md.

Development

Python 3.11+ runs the core tools and tests; GNU Make is optional convenience. The default checks and build need no third-party Python packages and no network access.

make check
make test
make build
make verify-build
Target Purpose
make help List every target; installs and starts nothing.
make doctor Report installed capabilities without starting hosts or native apps.
make check Validate source, links, identities, catalog, examples and inactive packaging.
make test Run all core tests in an isolated source copy; no network or native binaries.
make build / make verify-build Generate the shared plugin from allowlisted canonical files, then check it for drift.
make package / make source Create the deterministic plugin ZIP and the complete source ZIP, each with a checksum.
make release Ordered checks, core tests and reproducible packaging; no publishing or native acceptance claim.
make setup / make setup-probe Create a local .venv; then, as an explicit network opt-in, install the hash-locked official MCP SDK (mcp==2.3.0).
make test-sdk Exercise the real SDK against a synthetic stdio fixture, not the Craft apps.
make refresh-releases / make sign-releases The network steps the daily workflow runs (signing needs cosign).
make setup-confined Install, pin, probe and register the eleven root-confined apps on this machine.
make clean Remove only marked .build/ and dist/; workspaces and .venv stay.

Builds and tests never commit, push or install; only the explicitly named make github-* targets commit or push. The Makefile lists every target, and CONTRIBUTING.md describes the contribution rules.

Verification status

The offline core suite, the official MCP SDK contract test, strict Claude manifest validation, and Claude Code and Codex installation with Skill discovery have been run. setup has installed, probed and Sigstore-verified all fifteen Craft CLIs on macOS, Linux and Windows runners, and thirteen of them on a developer Mac as well. That is protocol-level evidence, not native acceptance: the gates in acceptance remain the operator's to run. The verification report separates what was executed for each release from documentary evidence.

Repository map

Path Responsibility
skills/craft/ One instructional Skill, fifteen app cards and two workflows
config/ Reviewed launch catalog, release manifest and Sigstore bundle store, inactive templates, example lock and env
storytold_tools/, storytold.py Deterministic CLI and optional short-lived SDK probe
scripts/, Makefile Offline checks, tests, guarded builds and packaging
tests/ Core regression tests, synthetic SDK fixture, native acceptance scenarios
docs/ Architecture, operations, acceptance, sources and verification
plugins/storytold/ Generated shared runtime; never edit it directly
.github/workflows/ Offline CI matrix and the daily release refresh, signing and three-OS verification

Architecture records why the native plan takes precedence over the older gateway reference and which component owns what.
